rubrics.justification: It correctly recognizes a blastocyst broadly consistent with 3AB, but it overinterprets the image by asserting a clearly compact ICM, specific TE gaps, debris, and a large vacuole/residual polar body that are not reliably identifiable from this single image.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, diagnosis, first-cycle status, and sperm parameters well, and relates these factors to prognosis, though some links are overstated.

The structure is logical and the probability estimate is internally explained, but several conclusions rely on speculative morphology and some quantitative adjustments appear more asserted than evidence-based.

SET, lifestyle counseling, and general prognosis discussion are guideline-consistent, but recommendations such as routine ERA, thrombophilia/NK/microbiome testing, and broad add-on investigations are not well supported for this first transfer scenario.

The response gives clear practical steps for transfer management and future planning, especially around SET and lifestyle modification, though some suggested tests/add-ons are not appropriately selective.
